changes.before: Replace include Named with extend Named but leave page.label unchanged. What happens?
changes.after: A module groups methods that other code can reuse. Include makes these methods available to instances of the class.

before: A module groups reusable methods without itself being instantiated like a class. include Named makes Named instance methods available to Page instances.

extend Named adds the module methods to the receiver as singleton methods. Writing extend Named inside the Page class body affects the Page class object, not Page.new. Neither operation copies method source into each instance.

This separate small example passes the Named module to extend on the Page class object. Its label method is then called on Page, not a Page instance.
```ruby
module Named
  def label
    "topic"
  end
end
class Page
  extend Named
end
puts Page.label
```
It prints:
```text
topic
```

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
module Named
  def label
    "topic"
  end
end
class Page
  include Named
end
page = Page.new
puts page.label
```
Expected output or behavior: topic. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: After the change, call Page.label instead and explain the receiver difference. You may trace it without a Ruby interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A module groups methods that other code can reuse. Include makes these methods available to instances of the class.
A new Page can now use the method defined in Named.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
module Named
  def label
    "topic"
  end
end
class Page
  include Named
end
page = Page.new
puts page.label
```
The output is `topic`. The page instance calls label and gets topic.
Compare extending the class itself with including methods for its instances.
